newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka seizes rebel arms ship, sinks boat.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka seizes rebel arms ship, sinks boat.

text.p: Sri Lankan armed forces seized a freighter suspected of smuggling arms for Tamil rebels and also sank a rebel boat off the northeastern coast, the Defence Ministry said on Monday.

Sunday's seizure off rebel-held Mullaitivu, the first of a suspected arms-smuggling ship in a year, coincided with a big army offensive against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), who are fighting for a minority Tamil homeland.
Air force aircraft fired on the freighter which was later escorted by navy fast-attack boats to the eastern port of Trincomalee, the ministry said in a statement.
Military officials said the ship's cargo hold was found to be empty, suggesting the crew might have unloaded the suspected cargo of arms.
The Defence Ministry said the pilots' suspicions were first aroused by the presence of a small boat near the freighter.
The boat was blown up with a rocket fired from a Pucara ground attack aircraft when the boat ignored warning shots and tried to flee, the ministry statement said.

Mi-24 helicopter gunships were sent to join the Pucara when Colombo shipping authorities could not confirm statements by the ship's crew that the vessel was the Cyprus-registered Caribbean Queen with 28 Cubans on board, sailing from India to Colombo for bunkering, the statement said.

The vessel was fired on and compelled to stop for identification and search after it suddenly started the engine and tried to sail away, despite warning shots, it said. The crew had originally said the vessel had engine trouble.
None of the freighter's Cuban crew was hurt, military officials said.
The home port of the freighter and other details of the ship were not immediately known.
The LTTE's Paris-based international spokesman, Lawrence Thilakar, was not immediately available for comment but another LTTE official in Paris said he was unaware of the incident.
The navy and air force have stepped up coastal patrols around this Indian Ocean island to intercept ships ferrying arms to the LTTE.

Earlier on Sunday, the navy and air force sank two LTTE radar-picket boats, used to monitor the navy's movements, near the island of Iranaitivu off Mannar on the northwest coast. At least 10 LTTE rebels were believed killed, officials said.
Monday's state-run evening daily The Observer reported that the two boats were returning from southern India with high-ranking rebels on board.
The LTTE maintains a presence in south India's Tamil Nadu state, which served as their rear base during the early phase of their struggle in the 1980s.
Meanwhile, Tamil rebels raided the key northern government outpost of Vavuniya on Sunday evening, wounding two policemen and four civilians, Vavuniya military officials said.

It was the third reported rebel attack in three days on Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo, from where government troops, backed by tanks, artillery and air support, launched a major offensive against the Tigers last week.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year.
